title: Hosted Mosaic Endpoints — Behavioral Contracts, Acceptance Criteria, and Launch Playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Define a single PRD and release playbook for a group of hosted inference surfaces (generation/chat/completions, embeddings, rerank) treated as a cohesive ‘Mosaic’ product. The goal is to provide a concise behavioral contract per surface, deterministic acceptance criteria, and an operational launch checklist that ties telemetry gates to rollout automation. Scope: Minimal viable behavioral guarantees for GA: semantic consistency for embeddings (unit tests + regression sets), prompt/response shape guarantees for chat/completions (including streaming and tool-calling compatibility), and ranked output stability for rerank. Excluded: SDK language-level ergonomics, long-term pricing experiments, on-prem private-pack distribution (handled by Private team).
acceptance_criteria: API contract: All surfaces conform to the unified open-schema: request/response top-level fields (id, model, input_meta, output_meta, tokens_consumed) and documented error codes — verified by contract tests in CI.

Functional: Chat/completions return consistent structured outputs for the 100 canonical prompts in the PRD testset; streaming yields the same final payload as non-streaming within 50ms post-final-token in 95th percentile latency on staging.
Embedding quality: Average cosine similarity delta to baseline model < 0.03 across three representative datasets (search, clustering, recommendations). Regression alerts fire if delta > 0.05.
Rerank stability: Top-5 reordering rate across identical inputs must be < 4% versus canary baseline; A/B evaluation page tracks per-query drift.
Latency SLOs: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for short prompts (<64 tokens) on hosted-1 region; p99 <= 1.2s. Embedding bulk endpoints complete 100 vectors/request under 2s p95.
Cost & qps: Throughput measured at 10k tokens/s sustained for a single dedicated instance type; autoscaling triggers validated in staging under controlled load.
Safety & errors: Rate-limited and quota-exceeded responses use consistent 429/403 patterns; unknown model/unsupported param returns 400 with guidance; all error payloads include request_id.
Operational: Telemetry dashboards show token consumption, median latency, error-rate, and model-fallbacks. All dashboards must display pre-defined signals and be accessible to SRE and Product.
Security: Customer request logs are redacted/PII-masked for hosted mode; KMS key usage metrics appear in audit logs for any encryption operations.
Documentation: Public API reference, quickstart examples for chat/embeddings/rerank, and a migration guide for legacy endpoint names must be published and linked from the console before GA.
Canary rollback: Automated policy triggers and a documented rollback runbook exist and are exercised in a tabletop prior to 50% rollout.
End-to-end test coverage: Contract tests, quality regression suites, and canary validation steps included in CI pipeline with pass/fail gates scripted in the release job.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal Preview: deploy to staging region; limited to internal API keys; run full PRD testset; duration 1 week.
Phase 1 - Developer Beta: expose to early customers via feature flag; monitor telemetry and run weekly quality evaluations; duration 2 weeks.
Phase 2 - Canary: 5% live traffic with automated rollback triggers; run real-time rerank drift checks and embedding regression monitors; duration 3 days to 1 week depending on signals.
Phase 3 - Gradual Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 24-hour observation windows between increments; tie each increment to telemetry gates.
Phase 4 - GA: flip feature default; publish GA docs and send customer communications; begin post-GA retrospective and 30-day quality baseline monitoring.
launch_checklist: Contract tests green in main CI for all surfaces
Canary dashboards created and tabled with SRE/PM/Design/Legal
Rollback policy and automation verified in staging
Public API docs and migration guide published in docs.redwood.ai/confluence
SDK smoke tests updated with new endpoint names and CI hooks
Telemetry: token-level cost, latency histograms, error categories instrumented
Alerting: error-rate > 0.5% or p95 latency breach triggers page and oncall
Security review completed and audit log sampling verified
Support runbook and FAQ drafted and linked from console
Legal/compliance sign-off for data retention and redaction policies
